bindiff: Find similarities and differences in disassembled code.
Usage: bindiff [OPTION] DIRECTORY
  or:  bindiff [OPTION] PRIMARY SECONDARY
  or:  bindiff [OPTION] --primary=PRIMARY [--secondary=SECONDARY]
  or:  bindiff --ui [UIOPTION...]
In the 1st form, diff all files in a directory against each other. If
the directory contains IDA Pro databases these will be exported first.
In the 2nd and 3rd form, diff two previously exported binaries.
In the 4th form, launch the BinDiff UI.

  Flags from this binary:
    --config (specify config file name); default: "";
    --export (batch export .idb files from input directory to BinExport format);
      default: false;
    --flagfile (comma-separated list of files to load flags from); default: ;
    --fromenv (comma-separated list of flags to set from the environment [use
      'export FLAGS_flag1=value']); default: ;
    --logo (display version/copyright information); default: true;
      currently: false;
    --ls (list hash/filenames for all .BinExport files in input directory);
      default: false;
    --md_index (dump MD indices (will not diff anything)); default: false;
    --output_dir (output path, defaults to current directory); default: "";
    --output_format (comma-separated list of output formats: log (text file),
      bin[ary] (BinDiff database loadable by the disassembler plugins). An empty
      value or using 'none' will disable writing to disk completely.);
      default: bin;
    --primary (primary input file or path in batch mode); default: "";
    --print_config (print parsed configuration to stdout and exit);
      default: false;
    --secondary (secondary input file (optional)); default: "";
    --tryfromenv (comma-separated list of flags to try to set from the
      environment if present); default: ;
    --ui (launch the BinDiff UI); default: false;
    --undefok (comma-separated list of flag names that it is okay to specify on
      the command line even if the program does not define a flag with that
      name); default: ;

Try --helpfull to get a list of all flags or --help=substring shows help for
flags which include specified substring in either in the name, or description or
path.
